spec: DESIGN.md — installations, the machine seam, save locations
description: Whole fixture machines (files, dirs, symlinks, core answers) in; the canonical contract serializations (atlas/contract.py) out, asserted with exact equality: installations (kind, kinds, root, health issue codes) and — per query — the full SavePlacement (dir, root_kind, needs, fallback_dir, physical_dir, file_set incl. completeness, granularity incl. option identity and alternatives, caveat codes + data), catalogue entries, and entry-route outcomes incl. Unresolved. Prose (sources, messages) is non-contractual. Layout facts are sourced from RetroArch runloop.c/configuration.c/config.def.h and the shipped RetroDECK/EmuDeck configs; see docs/research/retrodeck-save-placement.md.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sort-by-content-concrete
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK stock layout: cfg sets savefile_directory and sort-by-content. With a content path given, the placement is concrete: saves/<parent-dir-name>/. The existing save is observed, not guessed.

vectors.name: retrodeck-multi-disc-m3u-folder
vectors.rationale: The multi-disc convention: the ROM's parent directory is named '<title>.m3u'. content_dir is the parent directory name (runloop.c:8781), so the save lands under saves/<title>.m3u/ — observed on a real installation.

vectors.name: retrodeck-core-override-flips-sort
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK ships config/PPSSPP/PPSSPP.cfg with sort_savefiles_by_content_enable=false — a stock installation where the core override flips the layout flat for PPSSPP-libretro. The override directory is keyed by library_name (PPSSPP), resolved live from the core binary.

vectors.name: retrodeck-game-override-wins-over-core-override
vectors.rationale: The chain stacks core → content-dir → game, later wins (configuration.c:7095). The core override turns sorting off; the game override turns it back on — the game override must win.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sort-by-core-resolves-library-name
vectors.rationale: Sorting by core appends library_name — the core's self-reported display name (mGBA), not the .so basename (mgba). Resolved live via query_core through the /app→Flatpak-deployment translation; the existing save is observed through it.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sort-by-core-without-core-leaves-hole
vectors.rationale: Sorting by core needs library_name; without a named core the hole stays open (a hole is not an unknown — the caller can fill it), and a caveat states that per-core overrides were not checked.

vectors.name: retrodeck-savefiles-in-content-dir
vectors.rationale: savefiles_in_content_dir: the save lives next to the ROM. With the content path given, the directory is the ROM's own folder, concrete.

vectors.name: retrodeck-root-missing-health
vectors.rationale: The commonest Steam Deck failure: retrodeck.json is readable but points at an unmounted SD card. Detection reports health=root_missing instead of handing out a syntactically correct path as if usable.

vectors.name: retrodeck-no-query-detection-only
vectors.rationale: Detection without a placement question: retrodeck.json present, root exists, health ok.

vectors.name: emudeck-flat-layout
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck: settings.sh is the truth, the standalone org.libretro.RetroArch Flatpak is its RetroArch, the shipped layout is flat (sort keys false). One handle for both descriptions — no separate standalone installation.

vectors.name: standalone-flatpak-upstream-default-sorts-by-core
vectors.rationale: RetroArch's upstream compile-time default is sort_savefiles_enable=true (config.def.h:982). A bare Flatpak whose cfg sets only the directory sorts by core — the placement needs library_name.

vectors.name: standalone-flatpak-savefile-directory-absent
vectors.rationale: An unset savefile_directory means the RetroArch platform default — 'saves' under the config tree (platform_unix.c:2133-2134) — never the ROM's directory; upstream compile defaults then sort by core.

vectors.name: native-explicit-flat-with-observed-multifile-save
vectors.rationale: A native install with sorting explicitly off; the existing save is a core-written multi-file set (Beetle Saturn's .bcr/.bkr/.smpc). The file set is observed, never derived from an .srm assumption.

vectors.name: unloadable-core-is-stated-not-guessed
vectors.rationale: A core that is present but unloadable (missing host library — the applewin case) yields library_name unknown: the hole stays open and the caveat states it. Never a guess from the .so filename.

vectors.name: symlinked-save-dir-reads-through
vectors.rationale: A save directory reached through a symlink (RetroDECK's dir_prep pattern): the fixture resolves link prefixes like the kernel, so the observed file set is found through the link.

vectors.name: coexistence-retrodeck-and-native
vectors.rationale: Coexisting installations each get their own handle, RetroDECK first; no cross-installation fall-through and no silently chosen winner.

vectors.name: emudeck-claims-standalone-flatpak
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck is a configured org.libretro.RetroArch — the same RetroArch under two descriptions. One handle carrying both, never a second handle for the same installation.

vectors.name: nothing-installed
vectors.rationale: An empty machine detects nothing; an empty list is the truthful answer.

vectors.name: flycast-shared-vmus-in-system-directory
vectors.rationale: Flycast's default roots saves in system_directory, not savefile_directory: shared VMUs under <system_directory>/dc, one set for every game (rule card 'flycast', governing option reicast_per_content_vmus read live). Only the VMUs actually present are observed; granularity states the shared card and how to switch.

vectors.name: flycast-per-game-vmu-mode
vectors.rationale: The same core with reicast_per_content_vmus = 'VMU A1' switches to per-game VMUs rooted in the standard savefile_directory — granularity and root flip on one live-read option. Per-content applies to port A1 alone (oslib.cpp:40-41), so B1..D1 and the console flash keep using the shared card under system_directory: the save lies under two roots, which a card describing one cannot state. The file set therefore stays unknown and 'file-set-spans-roots' says why, instead of offering the single visible file as the whole save.

vectors.name: flycast-per-content-vmus-are-named-after-the-disc-id
vectors.rationale: reicast_per_content_vmus = 'All VMUs' writes one VMU per connected port into the save directory the frontend hands the core — the content-sorted one, no subdirectory of the core's own — named after the disc's product id (flycast@1dac369 oslib.cpp:38-67, libretro.cpp:2142-2148; live-verified on RetroDECK 0.10.9b). The id is written in the disc header, which atlas does not read: the file set is stated as the template it is and 'save_id' joins needs. Content without such an id — arcade, or a disc header stating none — is named after the ROM by the same function (oslib.cpp:62); atlas cannot decide which case it has, so 'filenames-content-conditional' carries both spellings, the alternative filled from the content path. A per-game VMU already lying in that directory is deliberately NOT attributed to this content — a content-sorted directory holds every game of one ROM directory, so reading a name back as this save would be a guess.

The opposite of savefile_directory, where a blank value keeps the standing root.

vectors.name: catalogue-declared-order-and-classification
vectors.rationale: The catalogue is read live from the bundled es_systems.xml in the Flatpak deployment: entries in declared order (first = ES-DE default), libretro entries carry their extracted core .so, standalone entries carry none.

vectors.name: catalogue-custom-overlay-replaces-system
vectors.rationale: A system defined in the custom_systems overlay replaces the bundled system of the same name entirely (ES-DE USERGUIDE, Game System Customizations).

vectors.name: catalogue-gamelist-selection-promotes-default
vectors.rationale: The user's saved per-system emulator choice lives in the gamelist.xml header as <alternativeEmulator><label> — written by ES-DE as two root elements (not well-formed XML, observed live). A matching label promotes that entry to effective default; the declared default stays as alternative.

vectors.name: catalogue-gamelist-selection-inside-gamelist-promotes-default
vectors.rationale: The same saved choice, written where ES-DE is moving it: <alternativeEmulator> as a child of <gameList> instead of a second root element (ES-DE reads both, document level first — GamelistFileParser.cpp:190-192; the nested shape is what RetroDECK 0.10.9b carries live). Where the element sits must not change which emulator atlas calls the effective default.

vectors.name: lrps2-shared-memcards-through-symlink
vectors.rationale: LRPS2's default (pcsx2_shared_memory_cards=enabled, libretro_core_options.h:169) keeps shared memory cards under <system_directory>/pcsx2/memcards. Under RetroDECK that path is a dir_prep symlink into the saves tree; the observed card is found through the link. The option's 'disabled' mode switches to per-game <rom_stem>.ps2 in the save directory (verified in libretro/ps2 source).

vectors.name: retrodeck-cfg-missing-platform-default-applies
vectors.rationale: A RetroDECK whose retroarch.cfg is missing: RetroArch initializes platform defaults before config load (platform_unix.c:2133-2134), so the effective root is 'saves' under the config tree — never the ROM's directory — and the upstream compile defaults govern sorting (sort_savefiles_enable=true, config.def.h:982).

vectors.name: entry-route-selection-to-placement
vectors.rationale: The natural client route: catalogue entry (with the gamelist selection applied) to its save placement in one ask. The promoted ParaLLEl entry resolves with its own core — the no-core caveat class does not exist on this path; the core is unaudited and the answer says so.

vectors.name: entry-route-standalone-is-unresolved
vectors.rationale: A standalone catalogue entry asked for its save location is a domain outcome with a stable code — outside current coverage, never a guess and never an exception.

vectors.name: secondary-handle-answers-its-own-config
vectors.rationale: Coexisting installations: the query names the native handle explicitly, and the answer comes from the native cfg alone — no cross-installation fall-through from the higher-priority RetroDECK.

vectors.name: retrodeck-marker-unreadable-is-present-and-broken
vectors.rationale: An unreadable marker is a PRESENT, broken RetroDECK — detection triggers on existence, and health separates the read failure from the root fallout instead of hiding the installation.

vectors.name: retrodeck-marker-invalid-json
vectors.rationale: Malformed JSON is not the same as an empty config object: the marker parses to nothing, health says marker-invalid, and the path fallbacks still answer.

vectors.name: sorted-dir-blocked-by-file-reverts-to-root
vectors.rationale: A file where the sorted directory belongs: RetroArch's mkdir MUST fail and it reverts to the unsorted root (runloop.c:8844) — the fallback is not conditional, it is the known answer.

files./mnt/sd/retrodeck/saves/gba: a file blocking the sorted dir

vectors.name: lrps2-dead-memcard-link-is-stated
vectors.rationale: The dir_prep link into an unmounted volume: the emulator-side memcards path is dead. The answer keeps the emulator-side directory and states the dead link with its target — physical_dir stays null because there is no existing backing path.

vectors.name: lrps2-memcard-link-cycle-is-stated
vectors.rationale: The other way a dir_prep link ends nowhere: the chain closes on itself, so the kernel answers ELOOP for the whole resolution rather than reaching any path at all. It is its own code next to dead-symlink because the two need different repairs — a dead link points at a name somebody can create, a cycle is one somebody has to break — and a consumer that branches only on dead-symlink to find an unwritable directory must miss this one. physical_dir stays null: there is no backing path, not even a half-resolved one to name.

vectors.name: emudeck-stale-marker-companion-missing
vectors.rationale: settings.sh survives while the claimed org.libretro.RetroArch Flatpak is gone: the EmuDeck handle stays (it claims the standalone identity), and its health exposes the missing companion config instead of silently suppressing a bare handle.

vectors.name: opera-per-game-nvram-subdir
vectors.rationale: 3DO NVRAM (rule card 'opera'): the core nests opera/per_game under the effective save directory it receives from GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY (runloop.c:2001/8977). The default mode is per-game; the file name carries the opera_nvram_version option, so the set is observed, never declared. The card was never live-verified on any arrangement — the answer says so.

vectors.name: opera-shared-nvram-subdir
vectors.rationale: The same core with opera_nvram_storage = shared switches to opera/shared with one card for every game — granularity and directory flip on one live-read option.

vectors.name: feature-detection-confirms-card-over-version-drift
vectors.rationale: The generation question decided by evidence, not version strings: the arrangement version drifted from the card's pin, but the probe shows the core REGISTERS the governing option with the card's value set — the card applies, no unverified-version alarm; the demotion is recorded in prose provenance (non-contractual).

vectors.name: multi-option-core-names-the-options-that-decide-granularity
vectors.rationale: SwanStation's audit verdict is multi-option: the directory follows the standard rule, but MemoryCards_Card1Type/Card2Type/UsePlaylistTitle decide whether the save is a per-game .srm, a serial- or title-keyed .mcd, or one card shared by every game. atlas does not interpret those options, so granularity stays null — and the caveat is what keeps that deliberate silence apart from a standard core's nothing-to-report, naming the options so a consumer can ask about them instead of assuming per-game.

vectors.name: standard-core-states-no-granularity-caveat
vectors.rationale: The negative control for the multi-option caveat, same layout and same empty granularity: mGBA's verdict is standard — RetroArch itself writes the save, per game, and nothing about the answer is being withheld. An empty caveat list here is what makes the multi-option caveat readable as 'deliberately unstated' rather than noise on every core.

vectors.name: standard-dir-core-observes-its-core-written-file-set
vectors.rationale: Beetle Saturn's verdict is standard-dir: the directory follows the rule and the file set is core-owned (.bcr/.bkr/.smpc, not RetroArch's .srm). No core option governs it — the shipped core registers none — so there is nothing deliberately unstated and no multi-option caveat: the files are content-keyed, the literal <rom_stem>.* observation reports all three, and the answer a per-game consumer reads is correct as it stands.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sandbox-override-dir-reaches-host
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK's RetroArch runs inside the Flatpak and writes its own spelling into the cfg: rgui_config_directory = "/var/config/retroarch/config", which Flatpak binds to ~/.var/app/<app id>/config/retroarch/config on the host (same inode, verified live). Translated, the stock config/PPSSPP/PPSSPP.cfg override is found and flips the layout flat; untranslated the whole override chain reads a directory that does not exist on the host.

vectors.name: retrodeck-sandbox-options-path-governs-card
vectors.rationale: core_options_path in the sandbox's spelling of the app config directory. The rule card's governing option is read from the file RetroArch would read, so the resolved granularity is shared-card; without the translation the file is invisible and the core default would stand in.

vectors.name: retrodeck-untranslatable-sandbox-path-is-stated
vectors.rationale: Same machine, but the override directory is configured under /var/db — inside the sandbox that is the runtime's own filesystem, which has no host location at all. The override cannot be read, so the sort-by-content layout stands, and the answer says why instead of presenting itself as complete.

vectors.name: ostree-home-under-var-is-not-a-sandbox-path
vectors.rationale: On an ostree host (Fedora Silverblue, Bazzite — both ship RetroDECK) /home is a symlink to /var/home, so real home directories live under /var. The machine's own configured directories must stay host paths there, while /var/config remains the sandbox bind of the app's config directory — which on this host resolves into that same /var/home. Both halves hold at once: the stock PPSSPP override is found through the sandbox spelling and flips the layout flat, and nothing is reported as untranslatable.

vectors.name: cfg-line-without-space-before-equals-is-dropped
vectors.rationale: A hand-edited cfg writes savefile_directory="…" with no space before the '='. RetroArch's key scan reads a run of isgraph characters, and '=' is one of them, so the key becomes the whole text and the line is refused (config_file.c:596-623): the saves root is NOT set, and the platform default under the config tree governs. Reading that line would attest a directory this RetroArch never writes to.

vectors.name: override-with-unknown-boolean-value-is-a-no-op
vectors.rationale: The core override spells sort_savefiles_by_content_enable = "yes". config_get_bool accepts exactly 1/true/0/false case-sensitively (config_file.c:1227-1262) and the bool loop writes nothing when it refuses (configuration.c:6412-6417), so the global layer's "true" still governs — the override does not turn the setting off. The rejected spelling is stated: nothing in the answer shows it otherwise.

vectors.name: cleared-rgui-config-directory-moves-overrides-one-level-up
vectors.rationale: rgui_config_directory = "default" clears the setting (configuration.c:6825-6826), and fill_pathname_application_special then falls back to the directory of the loaded retroarch.cfg (file_path_special.c:196-207) — one level above the platform default 'config' subdirectory. The override that governs is therefore <config dir>/PPSSPP/PPSSPP.cfg; the file in config/PPSSPP/ is the decoy that a wrong fallback would read.

vectors.name: app-relative-save-directory-is-stated-unexpanded
vectors.rationale: RetroArch's own config save writes ':' paths on some platforms: fill_pathname_expand_special resolves the prefix against the directory of the running RetroArch executable (file_path.c:1066-1101 → /proc/<pid>/exe, file_path.c:1421-1455). That directory is a property of the process, not of this disk, so atlas keeps the value as configured, states it, and does not run the existing-directory test on a path it would have had to invent.

vectors.name: unusable-override-save-root-keeps-the-global-root
vectors.rationale: The per-core override points savefile_directory at an unmounted card while the game override flips the sort. RetroArch merges the whole chain into one config and reloads the global cfg through it (configuration.c:7161-7243) WITHOUT config_set_defaults, so the value it refuses by path_is_directory (:6920) leaves the boot load's root standing - the global cfg's own /mnt/sd/retrodeck/saves, not the platform default. The rejection names the layer that stated it, because that is the file a caller has to fix.

vectors.name: override-switches-the-game-opt-layer-off
vectors.rationale: The per-core override sets game_specific_options = false. RetroArch reads that setting from the MERGED config: the core's retro_set_environment (runloop.c:5037) drives runloop_init_core_options and its settings->bools.game_specific_options read (runloop.c:1529-1530), one step after config_load_override merged the overrides (:5003). So the game .opt beside it is never consulted and the global options file governs - shared VMUs under system_directory instead of the per-game mode the .opt asks for. Contrast auto_overrides_enable, which is captured before the merge (:4941).

vectors.name: dropped-rgui-config-directory-line-moves-the-override-tree
vectors.rationale: rgui_config_directory is written with no space before the '=', so RetroArch's key scan swallows the '=' and drops the line (config_file.c:596-623). The override tree therefore stays at the platform default beside retroarch.cfg, and the PPSSPP override sitting in the directory the line names is never read - the answer keeps the global layout with nothing else to show for it. The dropped line is stated: it governs where every override and .opt file is looked for, so losing it silently would move the whole chain.

vectors.name: shadowed-override-save-root-is-not-the-fallback
vectors.rationale: Three layers set savefile_directory: the global cfg (valid), the core override (valid, and a real directory on this machine), the game override (an unmounted card). The chain is merged into one config before anything is read (config_file.c:768-805), so the getter sees ONE entry for the key - the game override's. The core override's value was overwritten in the merge and never reaches a getter at all. When the entry the getter does see is refused, the reload that refused it ran without config_set_defaults (configuration.c:7243), so what stands is what the BOOT load left: the global cfg's own value. A resolver that folds layer by layer answers with the shadowed core override instead, and is wrong on both keys below. Here that means /mnt/sd/retrodeck/saves, NOT the core override's /mnt/sd/other.

vectors.name: shadowed-override-boolean-is-not-the-fallback
vectors.rationale: Three layers set sort_savefiles_by_content_enable: the global cfg (true), the core override (false), the game override ("yes", which config_get_bool refuses - config_file.c:1227-1262). The chain is merged into one config before anything is read (config_file.c:768-805), so the getter sees ONE entry for the key - the game override's. The core override's value was overwritten in the merge and never reaches a getter at all. When the entry the getter does see is refused, the reload that refused it ran without config_set_defaults (configuration.c:7243), so what stands is what the BOOT load left: the global cfg's own value. A resolver that folds layer by layer answers with the shadowed core override instead, and is wrong on both keys below. Here that means the global 'true' governs and saves land in saves/psp, NOT the core override's flat 'false'.

vectors.name: archive-content-path-names-the-entry
vectors.rationale: Content inside an archive is named '<archive>#<entry>'. RetroArch cuts at the archive delimiter before truncating the extension (runloop.c:8702-8713, path_basename file_path.c:692-700), so the ROM is named after the entry, in the archive's own directory: the save of Pack.zip#Golden Sun (USA).gba is 'Golden Sun (USA).srm' under saves/gba, and it is observed.

vectors.name: archive-entry-name-finds-the-per-game-override
vectors.rationale: The game override is named after the same runtime basename (configuration.c:7095 reads config/<library_name>/<name>.cfg), so an archive entry only finds its override once the name is the entry's: this one switches sort-by-content off and the save lands flat in saves/, not saves/gba.

vectors.name: content-dir-observation-states-what-it-saw
vectors.rationale: savefiles_in_content_dir: the observation runs in the ROM's own directory, where everything the content consists of carries the ROM's name — the second disc track and the cover art match the same glob as the save. atlas states the whole set and says with a caveat that it may be wider than the save; filtering by extension would be a guess (REVIEW M10).

vectors.name: content-dir-root-and-sort-name-one-hole-once
vectors.rationale: With savefiles_in_content_dir and sort-by-content both on, RetroArch really nests the content directory under itself (runloop.c:8789 then :8827) — but the caller fills one value, so the template carries two positions and 'needs' names the hole once (REVIEW L4).

vectors.name: trailing-slash-content-path-names-the-same-file
vectors.rationale: A trailing slash disappears in RetroArch's own math: path_basename returns nothing (file_path.c:692-700) and the last dot is cut all the same (runloop.c:8710), so 'roms/psx/Game.cue/' is the same ROM as 'roms/psx/Game.cue' — same directory, same observed save (REVIEW L11).

vectors.name: content-path-without-a-name-is-refused
vectors.rationale: A path whose last component is empty and carries no dot leaves RetroArch's basename empty — it would write a save called '.srm' (file_path.c:345-358). Naming files after an empty stem would report every dotfile in the save directory as the save, so atlas observes nothing and states the refusal; the directory still resolves (REVIEW L11).

vectors.name: dotted-directory-truncates-the-way-retroarch-does
vectors.rationale: The truncation at runloop.c:8710-8711 cuts at the last dot of the whole path, guarded only by 'not at index 0'. An extensionless ROM under a directory whose name carries a dot is therefore named after the directory's first half, one level up — atlas mirrors it, because the answer has to name the file this emulator writes.

vectors.name: trailing-slash-content-path-keeps-the-content-out-of-the-set
vectors.rationale: Same machine and same ROM as 'content-dir-observation-states-what-it-saw', named with a trailing slash: RetroArch derives the same name from both (path_basename returns nothing, the dot is cut all the same), so the answer must be the same down to the file set — in particular the content file itself stays out of it, which only holds if the slash is normalized on the filtering side too.

vectors.name: per-game-selection-stops-at-the-game-that-declares-it
vectors.rationale: The live psx gamelist's shape (RetroDECK 0.10.9b): a root-level ./<name>.m3u carrying the <altemulator>, a <folder> of the same name, and inside it a second <name>.m3u carrying none. Gamelist paths are relative to the system's ROM directory, so they are resolved against it and compared as whole paths — matched by suffix at any depth, the nested namesake inherits a selection ES-DE would never give it: a promoted first entry for the wrong emulator, and a per-game-override caveat on a game that carries no override.

vectors.name: per-game-selection-reaches-the-game-that-declares-it
vectors.rationale: The other half of the anchor: the same machine asked about the game the <altemulator> is written on. Its emulator leads the entry list with the per-game provenance, and the entry route for a different emulator states the override the caller is about to contradict — anchoring must not cost the match it is there to place correctly.

vectors.name: retrodeck-marker-path-of-the-wrong-type
vectors.rationale: retrodeck.json is editable and its paths drive every read that follows, so a value that is not a path string makes the marker invalid — the same present-but-broken state malformed JSON produces. Handed on unchecked it reaches the seam as a path: os.stat reads an int as a file descriptor, so the answer can describe something that is not a path at all. The fallback roots still answer, and health says which state this is.

vectors.name: retrodeck-a-save-directory-that-cannot-be-listed-is-not-an-empty-one
vectors.rationale: The card is still mounted enough to be a directory and its contents cannot be read — the state a save directory reaches when the SD card starts failing. An empty file set here would be the same answer a genuinely empty directory earns, and a client acting on it would report the save as gone and offer to restore over it. The set is unknown, and the caveat names the directory that could not be read.

vectors.name: catalogue-that-could-not-be-read-is-not-an-empty-one
vectors.rationale: The shipped es_systems.xml cannot be read, so which emulators RetroDECK knows is unknown. The old answer was a bare empty tuple, indistinguishable from a catalogue that was read and declares nothing for this system — the same silent-empty failure the firmware route already refused. Both the per-system answer and the systems list carry the caveat, because the read that failed is the same one.

vectors.name: catalogue-a-bare-retroarch-has-none-and-says-so
vectors.rationale: An established fact about the arrangement: RetroArch ships no frontend catalogue, so there is no launch entry to answer with and never will be. Every handle answers the catalogue question now, and answering it with a reason is what makes the protocol honest — a consumer no longer has to isinstance-narrow to RetroDECK and guess what the others would have said.

vectors.name: catalogue-an-emudeck-arrangement-is-not-established
vectors.rationale: The other kind of no-entries, and the distinction the two codes exist for. EmuDeck installs a frontend — ES-DE, Pegasus or Steam ROM Manager — so it may well have a catalogue; atlas has not established where. That is a statement about atlas, not about the machine, and a client reading it as "no emulators" would be told something nobody checked. Distinct code, never the arrangement-has-none one.

vectors.name: catalogue-an-overlay-alone-does-not-make-an-unread-catalogue-read
vectors.rationale: The custom_systems overlay reads fine and declares n64; the shipped es_systems.xml does not read at all. Only the bundled layer decides whether a catalogue was read, so both answers refuse and the entry the overlay declared is not handed out. The overlay is genuinely optional — RetroDECK ships it fully commented out, so it parses to zero systems by design and can never stand in for the shipped file; an answer built from it alone would look like a whole catalogue with the frontend's own systems silently missing. The firmware route decides the same way.

vectors.name: catalogue-the-named-handle-answers-not-the-first-one
vectors.rationale: Coexisting installations: the catalogue query names the native handle, and the native handle answers — its own settled 'this arrangement ships no catalogue', not the RetroDECK handle's 'could not read one'. The two refusals carry different codes, so an answer taken from the first detected installation instead of the named one fails this vector.

vectors.name: aggregate-every-installation-answers-with-its-own-config
vectors.rationale: Asking every installation instead of choosing one: a machine carrying RetroDECK and a native RetroArch answers the same save question twice — the card root the RetroDECK cfg names, the home root the native cfg names — each labelled with the handle that produced it, in detection order. Nothing is merged and nothing is preferred: an answer that carried only the first installation's placement, or one placement for both labels, fails this vector.

vectors.name: aggregate-each-arrangement-states-its-own-catalogue-refusal
vectors.rationale: The labels are load-bearing. Asked the same catalogue question, the two arrangements refuse for different reasons — RetroDECK could not read the catalogue it has, the native install ships none at all — and both refusals survive the fan-out. Collapsing them into one answer would report a claim about atlas as a fact about the machine, or the reverse.

vectors.name: aggregate-a-single-installation-machine-answers-once
vectors.rationale: The ordinary machine: one installation, a one-entry aggregate. The caller gets a labelled answer without ever having chosen a handle, and the answer is the handle's own.

vectors.name: aggregate-an-empty-machine-answers-nothing
vectors.rationale: Nothing installed is a truthful answer, not an error: detection finds no marker, so the aggregate answers for nobody. This is the one expectation in the family that stands without a detected installation — asking every installation on a machine that has none is a question with an empty answer, not a question nobody can answer.

vectors.name: evidence-a-verified-and-an-unverified-arrangement-on-one-machine
vectors.rationale: The evidence caveat belongs to the arrangement, and one machine shows both sides at once: RetroDECK's placement was confirmed against a live installation and states nothing, while EmuDeck's is derived from upstream configuration alone and says so — same question, same machine, same detection order, two different evidence states. A caveat attached to the query rather than to the arrangement would appear on both answers; one attached to nothing would appear on neither.

vectors.name: health-findings-ride-directly-in-the-answers-caveats
vectors.rationale: A broken installation that still answers: the marker names a non-string path, so RetroDECK's roots fall back to defaults that do not exist, and the three findings — which marker key is invalid, which root is missing, which saves root — reach the placement as themselves, each under its own stable code with its own data. Nothing wraps them in a category code with the condition nested in data, and the same three findings serialize identically in installations[].health. The cfg still decides the directory: a broken marker degrades the answer, it does not replace it.

vectors.name: a-broken-unverified-arrangement-states-both-facts-in-one-list
vectors.rationale: Two features meet in one caveat list, and their order is the contract: the health finding first (EmuDeck's settings.sh exists and its bytes cannot be read, so the finding carries the path and the read status), then the arrangement's evidence caveat, then what the query itself could not resolve. A machine fact, a fact about atlas's evidence, and a missing argument are three different claims that must not merge, reorder, or crowd each other out — and the cfg still answers the directory, because an unreadable marker degrades the answer rather than replacing it.

vectors.name: a-broken-installation-states-its-findings-on-every-answer
vectors.rationale: One broken installation, three questions, three answers that all say so: the marker names a non-string path, so RetroDECK's roots fall back to defaults that do not exist, and the catalogue, the systems listing and the firmware answer each open with the same three findings in the same order. The point is that the findings are orthogonal to the answer: the cfg is still the truth, so the catalogue is read and names its emulator, the systems listing is populated, and the firmware root resolves — a broken installation degrades an answer, it does not empty it. An answer that stated the findings only where they happened to matter would leave a client reading the catalogue with no idea the installation is broken.

vectors.name: a-standalone-emulator-reads-the-same-on-both-routes
vectors.rationale: One machine, one standalone emulator, both questions: the placement route answers the typed Unresolved outcome 'standalone-unsupported', and the firmware route answers declaration 'unsupported' with the caveat code 'standalone-unsupported'. Same word for the same fact — the emulator is installed and atlas has no source for its rules — so a client that learned it on one route reads the other. It is not the evidence axis: nothing here was read and left unconfirmed, there was nothing to read.

vectors.name: firmware-an-absent-system-directory-resolves-to-the-platform-default
vectors.rationale: An absent system_directory is not a gap: RetroArch seeds 'system' under the config tree before it reads any config (configuration.c:5746-5749, platform_unix.c:2137-2143), so the firmware route resolves it and answers fully — the root, the core's declaration, and the BIOS found at that resolved path. It used to refuse this machine outright, which told a client 'no root to check against' about a directory RetroArch had already chosen. The card route has resolved it since item 14; this is the same fact answered the same way.

firmware_count = 1

vectors.name: firmware-a-cleared-system-directory-keeps-a-precise-refusal
vectors.rationale: The other half of the split: the key is present and cleared, which is not the same as absent. RetroArch then hands a core the content's own directory when content is loaded (runloop.c:1958-1997), so what the firmware root is depends on the run and no question here names content — the answer refuses, and 'system-directory-cleared' says precisely that rather than spelling it the way an absent key used to be spelled.

files./home/deck/.config/retroarch/cores/pcsx_:
display_name = "PCSX-ReARMed"
systemname = "Sony - PlayStation"
firmware_count = 1
firmware0_path = "scph5501.bin"
firmware0_desc = "PS1 US BIOS"
firmware0_opt = "false"

vectors.name: firmware-a-dropped-system-directory-line-is-stated-not-swallowed
vectors.rationale: The line the user wrote sets nothing — no space before the '=', so RetroArch's parser refuses it (config_file.c:596-623) — and the key is then absent, which resolves to the platform default. Both halves are in the answer: the root is the default one and 'cfg-line-dropped' names the line that tried to say otherwise. Silence here would be the worst of the two worlds this split created: the answer would look like an ordinary resolved one while the configured '/mnt/sd/bios' went unmentioned, and the BIOS the user put there would read as missing. The card route has stated this since item 14 for the same reason.

files./home/deck/.config/retroarch/cores/pcsx_:
display_name = "PCSX-ReARMed"
systemname = "Sony - PlayStation"
firmware_count = 1
firmware0_path = "scph5501.bin"
firmware0_desc = "PS1 US BIOS"
firmware0_opt = "false"
files./mnt/sd/bios/scph5501.bin: the bios the line meant to point at

vectors.name: catalogue-entry-caveats-carry-their-data
vectors.rationale: The system-level ask on a system whose gamelist carries a per-game override: every entry says so, and the caveat's data says how many games it is about — one, here. Bare codes could not carry that count, which is the whole difference between 'this answer may be wrong for some game' and knowing how much of the system it concerns. The entry also names its own system, so an entry that travels out of the call that produced it still says what it launches.
